newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: 100 dead or missing as cyclone hits Madagascar.
newsitem.headline: 100 dead or missing as cyclone hits Madagascar.

text.p: About 100 people were dead or missing and many homeless after a powerful tropical cyclone hit the Indian Ocean island of Madagascar, Radio Madagascar said on Saturday.
The radio said some towns had suffered 90 percent destruction as cyclone Gretelle hit the south-east of the island on Friday evening and again during the night, leaving thousands homeless.
The radio said the cyclone was the worst in human memory to hit the island's east coast.
The weather institute said it was 600 km (500 miles) wide and packed 220 kmh (140 mph) winds.
The towns of Vohipeno, Farafangana, Vangaindrano and Manakara were worst affected.
Residents called for help, saying floods swept away most food stocks, threatening shortages. The government despatched rescuers to assess the situation.
The port of Toliara, which was flooded two weeks ago by tropical storm Fabiola, was also believed to have been hit.
Gretelle crossed through the whole southern part of the island into the sea. It was the seventh storm to hit Madagascar since the beginning of the cyclone season last October.
